system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: PROMINENT NCT03071692 - Pemafibrate to Reduce Cardiovascular OutcoMes by Reducing Triglycerides IN patiENts With diabeTes (PROMINENT)
Investigational drug: pemafibrate
Document: The novel selective PPARα modulator (SPPARMα) pemafibrate improves dyslipidemia, enhances reverse cholesterol transport and decreases inflammation and atherosclerosis. (journal, published 2016-03-04, source pmid:27108950)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
The novel selective PPARα modulator (SPPARMα) pemafibrate improves dyslipidemia, enhances reverse cholesterol transport and decreases inflammation and atherosclerosis.

Background Atherosclerosis is characterized by lipid accumulation and chronic inflammation in the arterial wall. Elevated levels of apolipoprotein (apo) B-containing lipoproteins are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). By contrast, plasma levels of functional high-density lipoprotein (HDL) and apoA-I are protective against CVD by enhancing reverse cholesterol transport (RCT). Activation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-α (PPARα), a ligand-activated transcription factor, controls lipid metabolism, cellular cholesterol trafficking in macrophages and influences inflammation. Objective To study whether pharmacological activation of PPARα with a novel highly potent and selective PPARα modulator, pemafibrate, improves lipid metabolism, macrophage cholesterol efflux, inflammation and consequently atherosclerosis development in vitro and in vivo using human apolipoprotein E2 Knock-In (apoE2KI) and human apoA-I transgenic (hapoA-I tg) mice. Approach and results Pemafibrate treatment decreases apoB secretion in chylomicrons by polarized Caco-2/TC7 intestinal epithelium cells and reduces triglyceride levels in apoE2KI mice. Pemafibrate treatment of hapoA-I tg mice increases plasma HDL cholesterol, apoA-I and stimulates RCT to feces. In primary human macrophages, pemafibrate promotes macrophage cholesterol efflux to HDL and exerts anti-inflammatory activities. Pemafibrate also reduces markers of inflammation and macrophages in the aortic crosses as well as aortic atherosclerotic lesion burden in western diet-fed apoE2KI mice. Conclusions These results demonstrate that the novel selective PPARα modulator pemafibrate exerts beneficial effects on lipid metabolism, RCT and inflammation resulting in anti-atherogenic properties.
